result.title: EVA-Flow: Learning Shared Chemistry for Unified Environment-Aware Molecular Conformation Generation
result.comment: Accepted at Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), 2026
result.summary: Molecular 3D structures underpin simulations of thermodynamics, kinetics, crystallization, and nucleation, making their accurate prediction central to drug discovery and materials design. However, molecular geometry can change dramatically across environments. Existing models either ignore environmental effects or train separate models for each environment. We hypothesize that transfer learning across contexts is possible for conformer generation and that a general model will perform better when training data are limited, as in ligand binding and crystallization. We introduce EVA-Flow, a unified framework for environment-aware molecular conformation generation that learns shared chemical structure and adapts it through environment-conditioned generative modeling. Across vacuum, protein-ligand docking, solvation, and crystal packing, pretraining and cross-environment finetuning provide their largest gains in the three data-scarce settings. Evaluation against multiple reference conformations shows that EVA-Flow covers a broad range of solvation conformations. Analyses of molecules shared across environments support its ability to generate different conformations for the same molecule in different environments.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 EVA-Flow，一个按环境条件生成分子三维构象的统一框架，通过在真空、蛋白—配体对接、溶剂化和晶体堆积之间预训练与跨环境微调，共享化学结构知识并适应不同环境，重点改善数据稀缺场景。
